title: Dilatations of categories and commutative rings
abstract: Constructs categorical dilatations from sieves of permitted numerators and denominator morphisms, and proves their universal property for Sigma-regular functors satisfying the sieve containment condition. Develops restriction and union of centers, dual codilatations, and ordinary localization as a special case. The composition isomorphism retains the explicit Sigma-regularity hypothesis left open in the original paper. For commutative rings, an exponent-profile center recovers the ring dilatation; the naive single-index comparison is refuted over Z[X]. A finite category example refutes a general intermediate-category characterization. Independent ring modules provide fraction arithmetic, a universal property, reindexing, and the unique isomorphism for two-stage dilatations.

informal.CategoryTheory.Dilatations.Dila_universa: For a nonempty indexed center in a category C and a functor F from C to D, assume that localization of D at the images of the chosen denominators is faithful and that each pushed-forward numerator sieve lies in the sieve generated by its mapped denominator. There is a unique functor from the dilatation to D whose composite with the canonical functor from C is F.
informal.CategoryTheory.Dilatations.Iso315: The successive dilatation at Z and the pushforward of W is isomorphic to the dilatation at the combined center Z.sum W, assuming that the composite canonical functor to the successive dilatation is Sigma-regular for Z.sum W. This regularity is an explicit hypothesis, not a theorem of the development.
informal.CategoryTheory.Dilatations.Iso318: For two families of numerator sieves with the same denominator morphisms, dilating at their combined two-copy center is isomorphic to dilating at the pointwise union of the sieves.
informal.CategoryTheory.Dilatations.Prop51.Iso51: For any multicenter in a commutative ring A, the categorical dilatation of the multiplicative one-object category of A at all finitely supported exponent profiles is isomorphic to the one-object category of the ring dilatation A[M]. At profile nu, the denominator is the product of a_i raised to nu_i and the numerator ideal is the product of (M_i + (a_i)) raised to nu_i.
informal.CategoryTheory.Dilatations.NaiveCenterCo: For A = Z[X], ideal (X), and denominator 2, there is no equivalence from the categorical dilatation at the naive one-index center to the one-object category of the ring dilatation that commutes strictly with the canonical functors from the base category.
informal.CategoryTheory.Dilatations.Fact52.no_rea: The constructed category with three arrows from X to Y admits no equivalence to a dilatation of the base category with two such arrows that commutes strictly with the canonical base functors. This is an explicit counterexample, not a classification of intermediate categories up to arbitrary equivalence.
informal.CategoryTheory.Dilatations.iteratedDilat: For a multicenter M in any commutative ring A and any subset K of its indices, first dilate along K and then along the complementary ideals and denominators mapped to the first-stage ring. There is exactly one isomorphism of algebras over the first-stage ring from this two-stage dilatation to A[M], compatible with its canonical map.
